lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: determining where a text leaves matters uncertain

rubric.description: The response distinguishes what the text establishes from what it leaves uncertain.
Evidence is drawn from 11-CCR material and is quoted or located precisely enough to check.
The learner states what additional evidence would settle the open question.

scoringAuthority.scoringGuidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

acceptableAnswerCriteria.text: The response distinguishes what the text establishes from what it leaves uncertain. Evidence is drawn from 11-CCR material and is quoted or located precisely enough to check. The learner states what additional evidence would settle the open question. Evidence should be traceable to the assigned/selected text (a quote, a paraphrase with location, or a specific detail) rather than a general impression. Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.

masteryCriteria.rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one on 11-CCR material, including an account of what remains uncertain.

authorshipPolicy: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
doNotUse: Do not write, dictate, outline, or complete the learner's response.
This rubric describes what to look for, not a single required answer — accept any response that meets the criteria.
